transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-08-04 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Riley Morgan (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Asha Rao (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (NorthBridge Head of Platform), Marcus Epps (NorthBridge SRE), Priya Shah (NorthBridge Security), Oliver Kim (NorthBridge Backend)

Summary (auto): Quick deep-dive into Redwood Console request lifecycle, tracing, request logs and error forensics. Demoed request timeline, trace links between model calls + prefix cache, showed fallback routing, and discussed security/retention constraints for health-care PII. Agreed next steps to send security docs, sample trace export and schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics: request lifecycle, trace correlations, playback/replay, KV cache confusion, SLOs and fallbacks, private deployment audit trail, exportable trace format.

Transcript:
[00:00] Riley: Alright, starting on time — hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the request lifecycle in the console and then jump into a small lab where we look at an error blast you saw last week. sound good?
[00:08] Lena: Yeah that's perfect, we want to see how to get from a user event to the model call and how to quickly find root cause. last week was messy.
[00:15] Sanjay: I'll share my screen in a sec, heads up minds: the console view has two primary flows — timeline + request inspector — sometimes people call it traceplay or request replay in other tools so you might hear me say both.
[00:25] Marcus: also i'm most interested in how to attribute cost back to token budgets per route, and the latency spikes we saw on 7/28.
[00:32] Riley: good call — we'll show token breakdown too, quick reminder this is hosted demo account with synthetic data, not your prod.
[00:38] Sanjay: (screen) ok, starting at the Request Overview — you'll see request id, route, and attached trace id. click trace id opens the trace map.
[00:45] [00:45] Sanjay: the trace map shows spans for pre-processing, model infer, KV cache hit/miss, and post-processing functions. notice we annotate fallbacks — e.g., when the primary fp16 model wasn't available it routed to a quantized variant.
[00:58] Lena: hmm I think in our infra the term quantized is actually Q4, we might have a naming mismatch in the trace, will that break our automations?
[01:06] Sanjay: good note — the console tags are configurable, we can map your model aliasing server-side so your automation still recognizes the variant names.
[01:14] [01:14] Riley: question for Priya — what level of retention and export do you need for audits? that affects how we present the traces and PII scrubbing.
[01:22] Priya: we need at least 90 days of trace metadata for compliance and the ability to export redacted payloads. also need KMS-backed encryption and HSM for key rollovers.
[01:30] Asha: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for on-prem / VPC, we'll include that in the security pack.
[01:36] [01:36] Sanjay: jumping into an example request — here was the 7/28 spike. see this cluster of model infers — notice the KV cache miss at 14:22:13, each miss causes a ~120ms bump and then the per-token time spikes.
[01:49] Marcus: what causes the KV cache misses? do we need larger cache or a different TTL?
[01:55] Sanjay: could be two things — cache sharding leading to coldness after scale-up, or keys evicted due to memory pressure. console shows eviction alerts and per-host cache fill. you can configure the TTL and pin prefixes for critical routes.
[02:10] [02:10] Oliver: can the console correlate which upstream requests caused cache invalidation? we have a background job that wipes prefixes on deploys.
[02:18] Sanjay: yes the trace annotation includes upstream deploy events if you forward deploy webhook events — we can also ingest your CI job IDs to correlate.
[02:25] [02:25] Riley: sanjay, show them the request inspector and playback.
[02:27] Sanjay: sure — playback is not a full replica of the model outputs (privacy) but it replays the request path including headers, tokens counts, and timing. we redacted user PII but show hashes so you can link.
[02:40] [02:40] Sanjay: playing the earlier error — the post-processing lambda threw a parse exception and then the request retried twice which pushed it over SLO. see the retry span here and the error bubble.
[02:50] Lena: is that retry automatic by Redwood or our client lib?
[02:54] Sanjay: Redwood has configurable client retry policies for short transients; if you prefer strict no-retry for some routes you can set per-route retry=0.
[03:03] [03:03] Marcus: curious about cost visibility — can we see token delta per attempt and how retries increase charge?
[03:10] Riley: yes token-level billing is in console, you can filter by attempt id. we'll show a CSV export too.
[03:16] [03:16] Sanjay: note sometimes transcription in the logs shows model names slightly different (we saw 'redwood-mini' vs 'redwood-mini-q4'), that's from the model alias mapping; the mapping is surfaced in the model catalog.
[03:29] [03:29] Priya: security question — when exporting traces what fields are redacted and can we supply custom scrubbing rules?
[03:36] Sanjay: yes custom scrubbing rules are supported, regex-based scrubbing and structured fields can be redacted before leaving the VPC. on Redwood Private we can do in-line scrubbing with your KMS.
[03:47] [03:47] Riley: a quick aside: some customers tried to stitch our trace ids into Splunk but connectors will need to translate timestamp formats; we'll share a connector snippet.
[03:56] Marcus: please do, that would save us time.
[03:59] [03:59] Sanjay: moving on to error grouping — console auto-groups similar stack traces and shows a representative sample. here we see the parse error group which affected ~230 requests. you can click into the group to get sample payloads and upstream headers.
[04:12] Lena: are the sample payloads stored raw? we need them hashed.
[04:16] Sanjay: raw payloads are an opt-in export; by default console stores only metadata + hashed IDs for redaction safety.
[04:24] [04:24] Oliver: show the trace correlation across services -> e.g. client -> routing -> model -> downstream notification service.
[04:29] Sanjay: yes — here's the hop-map, we stitch IDs across services using the trace-context header. note: if you don't propagate trace-context, we rely on inferred correlation which is less precise.
[04:41] [04:41] Riley: question from our side — what's your timeline to production for this pilot?
[04:45] Lena: we'd like a two-week pilot starting mid-August, then a production rollout by Oct if results are good.
[04:52] Riley: that's reasonable; pilot typically runs on a dedicated tenant with sample traffic and 50k-100k request window for baselining.
[05:00] [05:00] Sanjay: demoing fallback policies — here's where you can set route-level fallbacks: route policy says prefer low-latency variant, fallback to cheaper quantized model on capacity failure, or degrade quality and notify. the trace includes the decision reason.
[05:14] Marcus: how are fallbacks encoded in the SLA / billing? we don't want surprise costs.
[05:19] Riley: fallback events are labeled and included in billing exports; we can also cap billed tokens for pilot if you want budget safety.
[05:26] [05:26] Priya: can we restrict exporting traces outside the VPC? for compliance we'd like server-side only and manual pull.
[05:32] Asha: yes on Dedicated or Private you can restrict exports and require signed requests for any trace dump. we'll document that.
[05:39] [05:39] Sanjay: small gotcha: when people try to do offline replays to reproduce nondeterministic model outputs, they sometimes forget the temperature/seed in the trace metadata — console preserves those fields but if you have custom sampling in a proxy you'll need to forward them.
[05:53] Oliver: noted.
[05:55] [05:55] Riley: ok last section quick Q&A and we'll recap actions.
[06:00] Lena: two questions — 1) can we ship event-level alerts to our PagerDuty for error groups? 2) is there an API to fetch grouped errors?
[06:09] Sanjay: yes to both - alerting hooks exist (Slack, PagerDuty, webhooks) and the API returns grouped errors with query filters.
[06:16] [06:16] Marcus: one more: if a model variant is unavailable and fallback triggers, will tracing show which region handled the fallback?
[06:22] Sanjay: yes region and instance id are included in spans.
[06:25] [06:25] Riley: cool, recap and next steps — we'll send security pack and SOC2 docs, Sanjay will export a 10k-request trace and highlight the cache misses/errors, Marcus will confirm sensitive routes list, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff on Aug 10.
[06:39] Lena: thanks, that's helpful.
[06:41] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll review the security docs when you send them.
[06:45] [06:45] Riley: thanks all — we'll follow up in email.

Notes & Links:
- Security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.example/security-pack
- Sample trace export (to be shared): s3://redwood-exports/northbridge/trace-sample-2027-08-04.ndjson
- Connector snippet for Splunk/ELK will be attached to the CRM record.

End of transcript.
